ai.description: *Uraeotyphlus menoni* is a slender caecilian reaching 20–25 cm. It is dark brown dorsally with a paler venter and possesses a distinct tail and visible primary annuli.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uraeotyphlus menoni* is uniquely distinguished from other Indian caecilians by the presence of a distinct, visible tail behind the terminal vent.
ai.habitat: *Uraeotyphlus menoni* inhabits moist, shaded soil within tropical evergreen forests and agricultural plantations in the Western Ghats, typically at mid-to-high altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Kerala caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and other small invertebrates in moist soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uraeotyphlus menoni* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs in underground burrows. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uraeotyphlus menoni* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically inhabiting moist forest soils at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kerala Caecilian produces a high-pitched, rhythmic series of clicks or chirps, typically heard while the animal is submerged in moist soil or leaf litter.
